story: Kukulkan is a serpent deity told about in several tales. In one, Kukulkan is a boy born as a snake. As he grows, it becomes clear he is the plumed serpent, and his sister cares for him in a cave. He grows so large that she can no longer feed him, so he flies out of the cave into the sea, causing an earthquake. To let his sister know he is still alive, Kukulkan causes earth tremors every year in July. In another tale, Kukulkan is a winged serpent who flies to the sun and tries to speak with it, but the sun, in its pride, burns his tongue. The same telling says Kukulkan always travels ahead of the rain god Chaac, helping to predict the rains, his tail moving the winds and sweeping the earth clean. Among another people, Kukulkan is portrayed as an evil, monstrous snake, the pet of the sun god. She destroys much of the world, then tries to kill herself during a long journey between life and death. During this journey she meets a boy who shares food with her; he follows her back to the human world, and she constructs her own country there.
